summary: Le Haillan is a commune of Bordeaux Métropole on the north-western edge of the Bordeaux area, partly covered by the Bordeaux Aéroparc business zone, which employed about 36,600 people at the end of 2017. Its parking story is mostly about park-and-ride: the metropolis lists two sites in the commune, Cantinolle (620 spaces, tram D terminus area) and Le Haillan Rostand (204 spaces, tram A terminus), at flat daily prices of 3.50 and 4.50 euros on the metropolitan parking page read on 21 October 2026. A third site, Mermoz (366 spaces, 74 charging points), was inaugurated on 2 July 2026 on Bus Express line G. The low-emission zone applies only inside the Bordeaux ring road and lists neither Le Haillan site among its 11 park-and-rides open to unclassified vehicles. The commune runs its own on-street rules (a blue zone in the centre), but the town hall website was behind bot protection, so tariffs, resident rules and council decisions could not be verified.

items.text: Since 1 January 2025 Bordeaux Métropole's low-emission zone (ZFE) applies 24/7 inside the Bordeaux ring road (intra-rocade) and requires a Crit'Air sticker. Only unclassified vehicles (e.g. petrol cars registered before 1997) are barred, and they may still reach 11 listed park-and-rides; neither Cantinolle nor Le Haillan Rostand is among the 11 (page updated 13 January 2026). Whether Le Haillan lies inside the zone is not stated on the page; it names only the ring road as the boundary.
items.source_title: ZFE (Zone à Faibles Émissions) : ce qu'il faut savoir

items.text: The town's 2025 map (file uploaded November 2025) marks Le Haillan's street parking as either unlimited-duration or blue zone (limited duration), with per-street space counts such as 23, 55 and 61 spaces. The map gives no time limits or prices, and the town's own parking page could not be opened, so the rules in force are unconfirmed.
items.source_title: Plan de la ville du Haillan 2025 (PDF)

items.text: On the metropolitan parking directory, read on 21 October 2026, Cantinolle (Allée de Jallepont, 620 spaces) shows a flat 3.50 euros for stays of 1 to 10 hours and Le Haillan Rostand (Rue Adrienne Bolland, 204 spaces) a flat 4.50 euros. The directory is the Bordeaux Métropole 'Se Déplacer' site; the price categories are not explained on the pages.
items.source_title: Parc Relais Cantinolle / Parc Relais Le Haillan Rostand (Se Déplacer Bordeaux Métropole)

items.text: Both Le Haillan park-and-rides are listed in the Bordeaux Métropole directory (read 21 October 2026) with the TBM site given as operator website; the directory covers 100 car parks and says the TBM network has 28 park-and-rides. The pages show real-time free-space counts, which makes these sites measurable through the metropolitan open-data feed.
items.source_title: Les parcs de stationnement (Se Déplacer Bordeaux Métropole)

items.text: According to the directory (read 21 October 2026), Cantinolle has 620 spaces including 15 disabled spaces, 20 with electric charging and 16 motorcycle spaces (max height 2.9 m). Le Haillan Rostand has 204 spaces including 5 disabled and 5 car-sharing spaces plus 20 bicycle spaces, no charging spaces (max height 2.1 m).
items.source_title: Parc Relais Le Haillan Rostand (Se Déplacer Bordeaux Métropole)

items.text: TBM offers short-stay park-and-ride tickets of 2 to 5 days at 12, 15, 20 and 25 euros, each including a round trip on the network. Cantinolle is one of 11 of 28 park-and-rides offering them; Le Haillan Rostand is not in the list (page read 21 October 2026, undated).

Tram line D was extended by 5.5 km from Mairie du Bouscat to Eysines Cantinolle on 29 February 2020 (EUR 250m, nine stops and two car parks opened the same day). The tram stop is in Eysines; the Bordeaux Métropole directory gives the Cantinolle park-and-ride address as Le Haillan.
items.source_title: Bordeaux tramway Line D extended (Railway Gazette International)

items.text: Bus Express line G, 21 km from Saint-Aubin-de-Médoc to Bordeaux Saint-Jean and serving Le Haillan, was inaugurated on 1 June 2024; it targets 50,000 passengers a day and 18,000 fewer car trips a day, with 5-minute peak frequency to Saint-Médard-en-Jalles. The release says seven Bus Express lines are planned by 2027.
items.source_title: Communiqué de presse: Lancement de la ligne G, première ligne de Bus Express (Bordeaux Métropole)

items.text: A new park-and-ride at 57 avenue Pasteur, Le Haillan (Mermoz, line G) was inaugurated on 2 July 2026 with 366 spaces (10 reserved for disabled drivers), 74 charging points, 70 bicycle spaces and 14 motorcycle spaces, per a press article that cites Bordeaux Métropole. The metropolis then had 31 park-and-rides with over 7,500 spaces.
items.source_title: Un parc-relais de 400 places avec 75 bornes électriques vient d'être inauguré aux portes de Bordeaux (Le Bonbon)

items.text: The town's November 2025 map shows Le Haillan Rostand as the tram A terminus, Cantinolle as the tram D terminus with an underground passage giving tram access, and a Mermoz park-and-ride with planned opening in the first quarter of 2026 (it actually opened on 2 July 2026). It also shows an economic zone 'ZAE Mermoz' planned for 2027.
items.source_title: Plan de la ville du Haillan 2025 (PDF)

items.text: Bordeaux Métropole's street-charging network had 364 charging spaces at 146 stations in May 2025, run with the operator Freshmile. Since 6 January 2025 the tariff is 0.38 euros per kWh plus 4.00 euros per hour after 4 hours (waived 23:00-08:00 on AC points), capped at 48.00 euros after 14 hours. This is metropolis-wide context; no Le Haillan station is named on the page.
items.source_title: Recharger mon véhicule électrique (Se Déplacer Bordeaux Métropole)

items.text: The Bordeaux Aéroparc zone (part of Mérignac, Le Haillan and Saint-Médard-en-Jalles, 2,515 ha including the airport) had 3,000 establishments and 36,600 employees at the end of 2017, about 15% of the metropolis's private-sector jobs. The figures are from 2017 and the study does not discuss parking.
items.source_title: Insee Analyses Nouvelle-Aquitaine n° 95: L'OIM Bordeaux Aéroparc

Search budget ran out before searching regional press (Sud Ouest, actu.fr, which the search tool also could not query): no press statements on park-and-ride usage or saturation, the Mermoz official release, resident parking, Aéroparc employer mobility plans or the tram D / tram A extension toward Saint-Médard-en-Jalles were found.
No official source found for an Aéroparc-wide parking policy; the Insee study is the only Aéroparc source and says nothing about parking.
The Mermoz park-and-ride page on the Bordeaux Métropole directory was not located (not found among IDs 230-700), so its capacity rests on the press article only.
